Results.ReviewText: Bought this to replace an electric grill witch was, in turn, used to replace an old model 325grill.  The electric grill was OK but not up to the BBQ standard I had experienced with the Weber Gas Grill. The new Weber model  incorporated several improvements that were overdue and very useful.  For example 1- New ignition system, 2 - Searing addition, 3 - Much more user friendly gas cannister location and ease of use. 4 - Larger temp gage. The new Weber heats up very quickly and is easy to manipulate the meats being grilled.

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. It is normal for condensation to form inside the thermometer. It often goes away when conditions get dry enough, or the grill is run at a higher temperature for more than 20 minutes or so. When this happens, you can remove the thermometer from the lid and put it in a cup of dry rice for a day. 

However, if the condensation gets severe and you can’t see the needle or markings inside even after troubleshooting, please don’t hesitate to reach out to us directly. We are always happy to help. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: The grill is only a month old and I have used it maybe a dozen times. Overall the grill is very good.  Quality of materials is excellent.  Lack of hot spots are quite good compared to other grills I've had.  Clean up is fairly easy.  The only reason I can't give it five stars is the "Snap Jet Ignition" does not work as easily as advertised.  The first couple of times I lit the grill they worked flawlessly. Since then, it takes several tries to get the grill to light on each burner.  That being said, I am happy with my purchase and hope the grill performs well for years to come.
Results.Title: Almost Perfect

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are sorry to hear about the issue you are having reaching high temperatures quickly. 

It sounds like your grill is in a safety mode known as "bypass" which is causing the ignition issues as well as not allowing your grill to reach the correct high temperature. Your grill should easily be reaching 450-500F degrees. 
 
You can read more here:
https://www.weber.com/US/en/blog/burning-questions/why-wont-your-gas-grill-get-hot-its-probably-in-bypass-mode/weber-29816.html
 
A member of our Specialist team will reach out soon to assist with troubleshooting. Thanks for your patience and for choosing a Weber grill!
